evidence.note: Explicit early gates before any full run: verify script parses + count params (29.9M), then test quantize/save/load round-trip and confirm 29.65MB < 32MB budget. Size correctness locked before scaling — a concrete done-check per phase.

Ran a deliberate 50-iteration smoke test to confirm training works end-to-end, caught the abnormal init loss (33 vs ln(8192)=9), fixed init, and re-ran smoke test to verify the loss curve before committing to the full run. Clear baseline-first sequencing.

Derived the bytes/token→bpb conversion and fixed the eval metric before launching full training, then measured baseline val_bpb (1.24 at step 2000). Established a measured baseline before improvement phase.

Capacity↔size↔compute trade-off was explored (checking int8/int4 compression ratios for 36-44M models, throughput problems forcing dim changes) with backup checkpoints as fallbacks — but this was reactive experimentation, not a pre-ordered milestone frontier with planned branches.

Full grader-interface verification (load_model_for_verification, both forward signatures, OOD probe) was run only near the END rather than front-loaded before capacity scaling; only the size gate was locked early.

reasoning: The agent clearly exhibits baseline-first decomposition (anchor 5): small model → verify save/load/quantize under budget → smoke test → measure baseline val_bpb → improve, each with concrete done-checks. It exceeds 5 because early gates were genuinely concrete (param count, quant round-trip, size < 32MB, smoke-test loss sanity) and size correctness was locked before scaling. It falls short of 8 because the full grader-interface/forward-contract gates were verified late rather than before capacity scaling, and short of 10 because the capacity↔size↔compute trade-off was managed reactively (improvised int4/bigger-model attempts with backups) rather than as pre-ordered decisions with planned fallback branches. This places it at 7.
